Figure 9: (a) Due to the sparsity of non-zero samples in the VP dimension, AesRM-CoT is prone to reward hacking: it may correctly identify differences between the video pair (e.g., Video B has richer details) but still outputs a score of 0. (b) We therefore design an asymmetric scoring strategy: for criteria where the teacher assigns a non-zero score, the student is encouraged to output a non-zero score rather than 0 through asymmetric rewards for non-zero vs. zero predictions. This strategy improves AesRM-CoT’s accuracy on non-zero VP samples and substantially alleviates score collapse.
